**Steps:** Security Store > Security agents > **Explore agents** > filter by product, publisher or rating > open the agent > **Get solution** > choose the billing subscription, resource group and a purchase name > if the agent uses Sentinel data lake resources, select a Sentinel workspace > review the terms > **Place order** > **Open Microsoft Security Copilot** to configure it.

**Partner agents and approval:** if a partner agent reaches Microsoft products (Intune, Entra, Sentinel, Defender, Threat Intelligence) through Microsoft skills, a **Global Administrator must approve its permissions**. Until then, **Set up** is disabled. Owners or contributors send the approval link, and the admin selects **Start approval**.

**Manage:** Security Store > Management > **My solutions** > View details. Agents also show up in the Defender portal for SOC scenarios.

terms.d: Microsoft security marketplace for agents, SaaS, content and services.
Starts the purchase and deployment of a Store offering.
Global Administrator step that grants a partner agent its permissions.

lessons.trap: When Set up is greyed out for a partner agent, the fix is Global Administrator approval of its permissions. More SCUs or a Copilot owner role won't help.
lessons.example: A SOC buys a partner enrichment agent through Security Store with its Azure subscription. The Global Administrator approves it, and an owner finishes setup in Security Copilot.

questions.stem: Administrators should hold the Global Administrator role only when they need it, for a limited time, after completing MFA. Which feature should you implement?
options: Eligible assignments in Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
A Conditional Access policy with sign-in frequency set to one hour
Microsoft Entra access reviews for the Global Administrator role
An administrative unit containing the administrator accounts
questions.explain: PIM eligible assignments give just-in-time, time-bound activation with MFA. Sign-in frequency only forces reauthentication; access reviews periodically confirm need but don't remove standing access between reviews; administrative units limit scope, not duration.

questions.stem: Which licence must cover users who have eligible role assignments managed by Privileged Identity Management?
options: Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium
Microsoft Entra Suite add-on for Microsoft 365 E3 only
questions.explain: PIM requires Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance for users with eligible or time-bound assignments and for approvers. P1 covers Conditional Access but not PIM; Workload ID Premium is for workload identities.

questions.stem: You are configuring PIM role settings for the Security Administrator role. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An approver for activation requests must also be assigned the Security Administrator role.
A ticket number entered during activation is validated against your ITSM system.
Activation can be made to require a Conditional Access authentication context.

questions.explain: Approvers need no role at all. Ticket information is only recorded, not validated. PIM supports 'On activation, require Microsoft Entra Conditional Access authentication context' to enforce CA controls such as authentication strengths.

questions.stem: A user needs just-in-time Contributor access to a subscription with approval required. Role settings are already configured. Put the steps in order.
options: Select the subscription under Azure resources in PIM
Add an eligible assignment of Contributor for the user
The user requests activation from My roles with a justification
An approver approves the activation request
Contributor becomes active for the configured duration
questions.explain: The resource must be selected in PIM before assignments are made; the user then activates the eligible role, approval follows because it is required, and only then do the permissions apply for the activation window.

questions.case: Contoso uses PIM for the Owner role on its production subscription. A recent review found that an attacker activated Owner after phishing a user's password and approving an Authenticator push. The CISO requires that activating Owner must use a FIDO2 security key or Windows Hello for Business. A Conditional Access policy can require the Phishing-resistant MFA strength.
questions.stem: Which PIM role setting should you configure for Owner?
options: On activation, require multifactor authentication
Require approval to activate
On activation, require Microsoft Entra Conditional Access authentication context
Require multifactor authentication on active assignment
questions.explain: An authentication context linked to a CA policy requiring Phishing-resistant MFA strength enforces FIDO2/WHfB at activation. The plain MFA toggle accepts any MFA method, including push. Approval adds a human step but not method strength; MFA on active assignment applies when an admin creates an assignment.

questions.stem: Two enabled Conditional Access policies apply to a user signing in to the Azure portal. Policy A requires MFA. Policy B requires a device marked as compliant. What happens?
options: Only the policy created most recently is enforced
The user can satisfy either policy to gain access
The policy with the narrower user scope takes precedence
The user must satisfy both MFA and a compliant device
questions.explain: All applicable Conditional Access policies are enforced together, so every grant requirement must be met (and a block in any policy wins). There is no ordering by creation date or scope, and 'require one of' applies only to controls within one policy.

questions.stem: You must measure how a new Conditional Access policy that blocks legacy authentication would affect real sign-ins over two weeks without blocking anyone. What should you do?
options: Set the policy state to Report-only and review sign-in logs or the insights workbook
Run the What If tool for each affected user
Create the policy in the Off state and review audit logs
Enable security defaults for the pilot group
questions.explain: Report-only evaluates the policy on actual sign-ins and logs the result without enforcing it. What If simulates single hypothetical sign-ins, an Off policy isn't evaluated at all, and security defaults can't be targeted to a pilot group.

questions.stem: Which TWO are Conditional Access session controls? Select TWO.
options: Sign-in frequency
Persistent browser session
Require password change
Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Require authentication strength
questions.explain: Sign-in frequency and persistent browser session are session controls that shape the session after access. Require password change, hybrid joined device and authentication strength are grant controls evaluated to allow access.

questions.stem: For each statement about Conditional Access, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Conditional Access requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence.
A single policy can use both Require multifactor authentication and Require authentication strength.
Conditional Access policies are evaluated after the first authentication factor is completed.

questions.explain: CA needs Entra ID P1. Require MFA and Require authentication strength can't be combined in one policy because the built-in MFA strength is equivalent. Policies are evaluated after first-factor authentication, so they don't restrict the first step.

questions.stem: A new employee has no password and must register a passkey on day one. Which authentication method should the help desk issue so the employee can sign in and register?
options: SMS sign-in
Temporary Access Pass
Email one-time passcode
Software OATH token
questions.explain: A Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode designed for onboarding and recovery so users can register passwordless methods. SMS and OATH need a method already registered; email OTP is for guest users, not member onboarding.

questions.stem: The help desk tries to issue a Temporary Access Pass valid for three days to a remote hire, but the lifetime is rejected. The TAP policy uses default settings. What should you do?
options: Enable one-time use in the TAP policy
Assign the help desk the Authentication Policy Administrator role
Purchase Microsoft Entra ID P2 for the remote hire
Increase the maximum lifetime in the TAP policy, which defaults to 8 hours
questions.explain: The default maximum TAP lifetime is 8 hours; it can be raised up to 30 days in the policy. One-time use doesn't affect lifetime, Authentication Policy Administrator configures policy but isn't needed to issue, and TAP needs no P2.

questions.stem: Which least-privileged Microsoft Entra role can create a Temporary Access Pass for a standard (non-admin) member user?
options: Authentication Policy Administrator
Authentication Administrator
Security Administrator
Global Reader
questions.explain: Authentication Administrator can create, view and delete TAPs for non-admin members. Authentication Policy Administrator configures the methods policy but doesn't issue passes; Security Administrator isn't a TAP issuer; Global Reader can view TAP details only.

questions.stem: Which methods satisfy the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength? Select THREE.
options: FIDO2 security key
Windows Hello for Business
Certificate-based authentication (multifactor)
Microsoft Authenticator push with number matching
Temporary Access Pass
questions.explain: Phishing-resistant MFA strength includes FIDO2/passkeys, Windows Hello for Business or platform credential, and multifactor CBA. Authenticator push is phishable, and TAP is accepted by the Multifactor authentication strength, not the phishing-resistant one.

questions.case: Fabrikam is rolling out passkeys. Compliance requires that passkeys be stored only on hardware the company issues (approved security key models and Microsoft Authenticator), never synced to consumer cloud password managers, and that Entra ID verify the genuine make and model at registration.
questions.stem: How should you configure the Passkeys (FIDO2) method?
options: Passkey profile allowing synced passkeys with attestation set to No
Conditional Access policy requiring a device marked as compliant
Passkey profile allowing only device-bound passkeys, with Enforce attestation and key restrictions by AAGUID
Authentication strength set to Passwordless MFA strength
questions.explain: A passkey profile with only the device-bound type, attestation enforced and AAGUID key restrictions meets all three requirements; synced passkeys can't be attested. Device compliance doesn't control credential type, and Passwordless MFA strength also allows Authenticator phone sign-in.

questions.stem: You want only members of the HR group to sign in to a SaaS gallery app. Where do you set Assignment required to Yes and add the group?
options: App registrations > API permissions
App registrations > Manifest
Microsoft Entra ID > Roles and administrators
Enterprise applications > the app > Properties and Users and groups
questions.explain: User assignment and the Assignment required property belong to the service principal, managed under Enterprise applications. API permissions and the manifest are part of the app registration, and directory roles grant admin rights rather than app access.

questions.stem: A software vendor publishes a multitenant app used by your tenant. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The application object exists only in the vendor's home tenant.
Your tenant has its own service principal for the app.
Deleting the enterprise application in your tenant deletes the vendor's app registration.

questions.explain: A multitenant app has one application object in the publisher's tenant and a separate service principal in each consuming tenant. Deleting your service principal removes the app from your tenant only.

questions.case: A development team deploys Bicep templates to Azure from GitHub Actions running on GitHub-hosted runners. Security policy forbids storing any long-lived credential, including secrets and certificate private keys, in GitHub.
questions.stem: Which credential should the deployment identity use?
options: A client secret stored as an encrypted GitHub secret
A certificate uploaded to the app registration
A federated identity credential on the app registration
A system-assigned managed identity on the runner
questions.explain: Workload identity federation lets Entra ID trust GitHub's OIDC token, so no secret is stored. Secrets and certificates are long-lived credentials kept in GitHub, and GitHub-hosted runners aren't Azure resources, so they can't have a managed identity.

questions.stem: After a consent-phishing attack, you want users to keep consenting only to low-risk permissions requested by trustworthy apps. Which user consent setting should you choose?
options: Allow user consent for apps from verified publishers, for selected permissions
Allow user consent for apps
Do not allow user consent
Allow user consent for application permissions only
questions.explain: The verified-publishers option limits consent to verified or in-tenant apps and to permissions classified as low impact. 'Allow user consent for apps' is the permissive legacy default; disabling consent blocks all; users can never consent to application permissions.

questions.case: Contoso set user consent to 'Do not allow user consent'. Users now see an error when an app asks for permissions and help desk tickets are rising. Contoso wants users to submit a justified request that the cloud application team can review and approve within a week.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions should you take? Select TWO.
options: Enable the admin consent workflow
Designate the cloud application team (with a role able to grant consent) as reviewers
Assign all users the Application Developer role
Classify every Microsoft Graph permission as low impact
Enable security defaults
questions.explain: The admin consent workflow lets users request access, and reviewers must already hold a role that can grant the consent. Application Developer only allows app registration, classifying everything as low impact defeats the control, and security defaults don't handle consent.

questions.stem: You are using Microsoft Graph PowerShell to allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers for permissions classified as low impact. Complete the command.
options: microsoft-user-default-low
microsoft-user-default-legacy
microsoft-all-application-permissions
microsoft-company-admin
questions.explain: microsoft-user-default-low is the built-in policy for verified publishers and low-impact permissions. The legacy policy allows consent to any permission not requiring admin consent; the other two are broader built-in policies used for admin-level grants.

questions.stem: You must attach an existing user-assigned managed identity named uami-shared to VM1 by using the Azure CLI. Complete the command.
questions.code: az vm identity assign --resource-group rg1 --name VM1 ____ uami-shared
options: --assignee
--identities
--assign-identity
--role
questions.explain: az vm identity assign uses --identities with the name or resource ID of a user-assigned identity (omitting it enables system-assigned). --assign-identity belongs to az vm create; --assignee and --role relate to role assignments, not attaching identities.

questions.stem: Twenty App Service apps that are frequently deleted and recreated must all read the same Key Vault secrets, and the vault permissions must be granted once before the apps exist. Which identity should you use?
options: A system-assigned managed identity on each app
A service principal with a client secret in app settings
A federated identity credential for each app
A single user-assigned managed identity assigned to all the apps
questions.explain: A user-assigned identity is a standalone resource that can be pre-authorised and shared, and survives app deletion. System-assigned identities are per resource and deleted with it; a client secret reintroduces a stored credential; federated credentials are for external workloads.

questions.stem: An application needs RSA keys protected by hardware security modules, stored alongside its secrets in a multitenant service, at the lowest cost. Which option should you deploy?
options: Azure Key Vault Standard tier
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
Azure Key Vault Premium tier
Azure Dedicated HSM
questions.explain: Premium vaults add HSM-protected keys (RSA-HSM, EC-HSM) and still store secrets and certificates. Standard holds only software-protected keys. Managed HSM is single-tenant and stores keys only; Dedicated HSM is a costly appliance with no secret store.

questions.case: A regulator requires Woodgrove Bank to keep encryption keys in single-tenant, FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs. Woodgrove must hold the recovery credential for the HSM so that subscription owners at Woodgrove cannot override the key administrators' permissions.
questions.stem: Which service meets the requirements?
options: Azure Key Vault Premium with Azure RBAC
Azure Key Vault Standard with purge protection
Azure Key Vault Premium with vault access policies
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
questions.explain: Managed HSM is single-tenant, FIPS 140-3 Level 3, uses a customer-held security domain, and its local RBAC can't be overridden by subscription administrators. Premium and Standard vaults are multitenant and governed by Azure control-plane roles.

questions.stem: You create a new key vault with the Key Vault control-plane API version 2026-02-01 and do not set enableRbacAuthorization. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The new vault uses the Azure RBAC permission model.
Existing vaults that use access policies are switched to Azure RBAC when updated with that API version.
You can still create a vault that uses access policies by setting enableRbacAuthorization to false.

questions.explain: From API 2026-02-01, create operations default to Azure RBAC unless enableRbacAuthorization is false. Existing vaults keep their current model; updates don't switch it. Both models remain supported.

questions.stem: What is the default soft-delete retention period for a new Azure key vault?
options: 14 days
30 days
90 days
180 days
questions.explain: Key Vault soft-delete retention is configurable from 7 to 90 days at creation, defaulting to 90. 14 days is Azure Backup's default soft-delete period, and 180 days is Backup's maximum, not Key Vault's.

questions.stem: A key vault has soft delete with 30-day retention and purge protection enabled. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A user with sufficient permissions can still delete a secret.
A Key Vault Purge Operator can permanently purge the deleted secret immediately.
Purge protection can later be disabled by the subscription Owner.

questions.explain: Purge protection doesn't prevent deletion; it prevents purging until the retention period ends, even for purge-capable roles. Once enabled, purge protection can't be disabled by anyone, including Microsoft.

questions.stem: You must configure an existing vault so that a storage account can use one of its keys as a customer-managed key. Complete the command.
questions.code: az keyvault update --name kv-prod-01 --resource-group rg-sec ____ true
options: --enable-soft-delete
--enabled-for-disk-encryption
--enable-rbac-authorization
--enable-purge-protection
questions.explain: Storage customer-managed keys require soft delete and purge protection on the vault; soft delete is already always on, so --enable-purge-protection true is the missing step. Disk encryption and RBAC flags don't satisfy the CMK prerequisite.

questions.stem: An ARM template parameter file references a VM admin password stored in a key vault. Deployment fails with an error stating the vault is not enabled for template deployment. Which vault setting should you enable?
options: Azure Virtual Machines for deployment
Azure Resource Manager for template deployment
Azure Disk Encryption for volume encryption
Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass this firewall
questions.explain: enabledForTemplateDeployment lets Azure Resource Manager retrieve secrets referenced in parameter files. The VM deployment flag lets VMs retrieve certificates, the disk encryption flag serves Azure Disk Encryption, and the firewall bypass doesn't change this permission.

questions.stem: A web app's managed identity must read secret values from an RBAC-enabled key vault and nothing else. Which built-in role should you assign?
options: Key Vault Secrets User
Key Vault Reader
Key Vault Secrets Officer
Key Vault Contributor
questions.explain: Key Vault Secrets User reads secret contents, the least privilege for an app. Key Vault Reader reads metadata but not values, Secrets Officer can also create and delete secrets, and Key Vault Contributor is control plane only.

questions.case: Tailwind Traders has a key vault that uses the vault access policy permission model. An operations engineer holds Key Vault Contributor on the vault so he can change networking settings. An audit shows he read a production database password last week, even though he was never given secret permissions.
questions.stem: What is the most effective way to prevent this while keeping his ability to manage vault settings?
options: Replace Key Vault Contributor with Key Vault Reader
Enable purge protection on the vault
Migrate the vault to the Azure RBAC permission model and grant data roles only to those who need them
Add a CanNotDelete resource lock to the vault
questions.explain: In the access policy model, Key Vault Contributor can edit access policies and grant himself data access. Under Azure RBAC, data access requires role assignments he can't create. Reader would block his settings work; purge protection and locks don't control data-plane reads.

questions.stem: Which TWO are advantages of the Azure RBAC permission model over vault access policies in Azure Key Vault? Select TWO.
options: Permissions can be assigned on an individual secret, key or certificate
Privileged data roles can be made eligible through PIM
It allows data-plane access without Microsoft Entra authentication
It removes the need for a firewall on the vault
It grants Key Vault Contributor full data-plane access automatically
questions.explain: Azure RBAC supports object-level scope and integrates with PIM for just-in-time access. Both models still require Entra authentication, neither replaces network controls, and Key Vault Contributor never gets data-plane access under RBAC.

questions.stem: A storage account uses a customer-managed key in an RBAC-enabled vault. The storage account's managed identity needs only to read key metadata and perform wrap and unwrap operations. Which role should you assign?
options: Key Vault Crypto Officer
Key Vault Administrator
Key Vault Crypto User
Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User
questions.explain: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User reads key metadata and performs wrap/unwrap, exactly what CMK needs. Crypto User allows all cryptographic operations, Crypto Officer manages keys, and Administrator covers all data-plane objects.

questions.stem: Applications in an Azure VNet must reach a key vault over a private IP address, and the vault must refuse all traffic through its public endpoint. What should you configure?
options: A private endpoint and set public network access to Disabled
A service endpoint on the subnet and a virtual network rule
An IP rule containing the subnet's private address range
Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass this firewall
questions.explain: A private endpoint gives the vault a private IP via Private Link; disabling public access rejects public-endpoint traffic. Service endpoints still use the public endpoint, IP rules reject private RFC 1918 ranges, and the trusted services bypass is for Microsoft services.

questions.stem: You must block all public traffic to a key vault except from approved networks while still letting trusted Microsoft services reach it. Complete the command.
questions.code: az keyvault update --name kv-app-01 --default-action Deny ____ AzureServices
options: --public-network-access
--bypass
--network-acls
--allow-trusted
questions.explain: --bypass AzureServices allows trusted Microsoft services through when the default action is Deny. --public-network-access only toggles Enabled or Disabled, and --network-acls and --allow-trusted don't set the trusted-services exception on this command.

questions.stem: A key vault's networking is set to allow public access from selected virtual networks and IP addresses only. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: You can add the IP range 10.20.0.0/16 as an IP firewall rule.
An ARM control-plane operation such as changing the vault's tags is blocked from non-allowed networks.
An administrator browsing from a non-allowed IP might be unable to list secrets in the Azure portal.

questions.explain: IP rules accept only public IPv4 addresses; private RFC 1918 ranges are rejected. Firewall rules apply only to data-plane operations, so control-plane changes still work. Portal listing of secrets is a data-plane call from the client, so it needs an allowed IP.

questions.stem: You are moving an app from public access to private-only access to its key vault without downtime. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a private endpoint for the vault in the app's VNet
Link the privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net private DNS zone to the VNet
Verify the vault name resolves to the private IP from the app
Set public network access on the vault to Disabled
questions.explain: The private endpoint and DNS zone must exist and resolve correctly before public access is removed; disabling public access first would cut the app off until private connectivity worked.

questions.stem: A SQL server uses TDE with a customer-managed key from Key Vault. You will enable automatic key rotation and want SQL to start using each new version without reconfiguration. What should you do?
options: Configure SQL with the versioned key identifier of the current key
Configure SQL with the versionless key URI
Disable the previous key version immediately after each rotation
Export the new key version and upload it to SQL after rotation
questions.explain: A versionless key URI resolves to the latest version, so the service picks up rotations automatically. A versioned identifier pins one version; disabling old versions too early can break unwrap; key material in Key Vault HSMs isn't exported.

questions.stem: You must apply a JSON rotation policy (rotate every 18 months, notify 30 days before expiry) to a key. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code: az keyvault key ____ --vault-name kv-cmk --name storage-key --value ./policy.json
options: rotate
set-attributes
rotation-policy update
create
questions.explain: az keyvault key rotation-policy update applies a rotation policy from a JSON file. 'rotate' performs an on-demand rotation now, set-attributes changes enablement or dates, and create makes a new key.

questions.stem: For each statement about Key Vault key rotation, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Rotating a key creates a new key version with new key material.
Data wrapped with the previous key version becomes unrecoverable after rotation.
Key Vault Crypto Officer can manage a key's rotation policy in an RBAC vault.

questions.explain: Rotation adds a new version and leaves previous versions intact, so earlier wrapped data can still be unwrapped while those versions stay enabled. Key Vault Crypto Officer is the role documented for managing rotation policies.

questions.stem: A public TLS certificate in Key Vault must renew automatically without manual CSR merging. Which configuration supports this?
options: Issue the certificate from a non-partnered CA and add an EmailContacts lifetime action
Import the PFX and enable soft delete
Store the certificate as a secret with an expiration date
Use an issuer object for DigiCert or GlobalSign with an AutoRenew lifetime action
questions.explain: Auto-renewal requires a partnered CA (DigiCert or GlobalSign) or self-signed issuer plus an AutoRenew lifetime action. Non-partnered CAs need manual renewal, EmailContacts only notifies, and secrets or imports don't renew themselves.

questions.stem: When you create a certificate in Azure Key Vault, which additional addressable objects with the same name are created?
options: A key and a secret
A key and a managed identity
A secret and a certificate issuer
Only a certificate policy
questions.explain: Key Vault creates an addressable key (for key operations) and a secret (to retrieve the certificate including the private key if exportable). Issuers are separate vault objects, and no managed identity is created.

questions.stem: You are automating rotation of a database password stored as a Key Vault secret. Put the steps in order.
options: Key Vault publishes a SecretNearExpiry event to Event Grid
An Azure Function subscribed to the event is triggered
The function generates a new password at the database
The function stores the password as a new secret version
questions.explain: Near-expiry events flow through Event Grid to the subscribed function, which first changes the credential at its source and then writes the new value as a new secret version so applications read the current password.

questions.stem: Your company enables only foundational CSPM (free) in Defender for Cloud. You need agentless scanning of Azure VMs for exposed secrets. Which plans would provide this? Select TWO.
options: Defender CSPM
Defender for Servers Plan 2
Defender for Servers Plan 1
Defender for Key Vault
Defender for Storage
questions.explain: Agentless machine secrets scanning comes with Defender CSPM or Defender for Servers Plan 2. Servers Plan 1 lacks agentless scanning, Defender for Key Vault detects suspicious vault access, and Defender for Storage protects storage data.

questions.case: Defender CSPM is enabled. The security team wants to see whether a plaintext storage account connection string found on an internet-exposed VM could let an attacker reach a storage account holding sensitive data, and to prioritize fixing it accordingly.
questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud capability should the team use first?
options: Regulatory compliance dashboard
Workflow automation
Attack path analysis
Just-in-time VM access
questions.explain: Attack path analysis chains internet exposure, the secret found on the VM and the reachable sensitive storage account into a prioritized path. The regulatory compliance dashboard maps controls, workflow automation triggers Logic Apps, and just-in-time VM access only restricts management ports.

questions.stem: You need alerts when a key vault is accessed from a TOR exit node or when an identity lists and then reads many secrets. What should you enable?
options: Microsoft Defender for Key Vault
Defender CSPM secrets scanning
Key Vault purge protection
Azure Policy built-in definitions for Key Vault
questions.explain: Defender for Key Vault detects anomalous access such as TOR, suspicious IPs and List-then-Get secret dumping. Secrets scanning finds exposed secrets on resources, purge protection protects deleted objects, and Azure Policy checks configuration, not live access.

questions.case: Defender for Key Vault raises 'Suspicious secret listing and query in a key vault' for a service principal that belongs to a decommissioned integration. The vault uses Azure RBAC and allows public access from all networks.
questions.stem: Which THREE actions should you take to contain and recover? Select THREE.
options: Remove the service principal's role assignments on the vault
Rotate the secrets the service principal read
Restrict the vault firewall to approved networks
Dismiss the alert because the service principal is known to your organization
Enable the vault's soft-delete feature
questions.explain: Removing access, rotating exposed secrets and restricting network access follow Microsoft's response guidance. A recognised identity isn't a reason to dismiss, and soft delete is already always on and doesn't address exfiltration.

questions.stem: You send Key Vault diagnostic logs to Log Analytics (AzureDiagnostics table) and want to find who read secrets. Complete the KQL query.
questions.code:
AzureDiagnostics
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT"
| where OperationName == ____
| summarize count() by CallerIPAddress, identity_claim_appid_g
options: "SecretList"
"VaultGet"
"SecretGet"
"SecretSet"
questions.explain: SecretGet records reads of secret values. SecretList only enumerates names, VaultGet is a vault metadata read, and SecretSet creates or updates a secret.

questions.stem: You need Azure Policy to automatically deploy a diagnostic setting to any key vault that lacks one. Which effect should the policy definition use?
options: auditIfNotExists
deployIfNotExists
append
deny
questions.explain: deployIfNotExists deploys a missing related resource through an ARM template using a managed identity. auditIfNotExists only reports the gap, append adds fields to the request itself, and deny blocks non-compliant requests.

questions.stem: Which Azure Policy effect can block the DELETE operation on resources that match a condition, while still allowing them to be created and updated?
options: deny
modify
denyAction
disabled
questions.explain: denyAction blocks specified actions such as delete on matching resources. deny blocks create and update requests, modify alters properties or tags, and disabled turns the rule off.

questions.stem: A custom policy must prevent creation of storage accounts that allow public blob access. Complete the policy rule.
options: "audit"
"deny"
"auditIfNotExists"
"manual"
questions.explain: deny rejects the create or update request when the condition matches. audit only logs non-compliance, auditIfNotExists checks for a related resource, and manual relies on human attestation.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Policy, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An initiative groups multiple policy definitions so they can be assigned together.
The modify effect requires a managed identity on the assignment to change resources.
The audit effect blocks non-compliant resources from being created.

questions.explain: An initiative (policy set definition) bundles definitions. modify and deployIfNotExists use the assignment's managed identity to make changes. audit only records non-compliance; deny is the effect that blocks.

questions.stem: You assigned a deployIfNotExists policy that installs a monitoring extension. New VMs get the extension, but 200 existing VMs remain non-compliant. What should you do?
options: Change the assignment's enforcement mode to DoNotEnforce
Create a policy exemption for the existing VMs
Create a remediation task for the assignment
Change the effect to auditIfNotExists
questions.explain: deployIfNotExists acts automatically only on new or updated resources; a remediation task applies it to existing non-compliant resources. DoNotEnforce stops enforcement, exemptions hide rather than fix, and auditIfNotExists only reports.

questions.stem: A VM is protected by a third-party disk encryption product, so it fails a built-in encryption policy even though the policy's intent is met. You want it shown as exempt with the reason recorded. Which exemption category should you use?
options: Waiver
Exclusion
DoNotEnforce
Mitigated
questions.explain: Mitigated means the policy intent is met through another method. Waiver means non-compliance is temporarily accepted. Exclusions (notScopes) silently remove scope rather than recording an exemption, and DoNotEnforce is an assignment enforcement mode.

questions.stem: You will roll out a custom 'deny public IP on NICs' policy across all subscriptions under a management group with minimal disruption. Put the steps in order.
options: Save the custom definition at the management group
Assign it at the management group with enforcement mode DoNotEnforce
Review compliance results and create exemptions for justified resources
Change the assignment's enforcement mode to Default
questions.explain: The definition must be saved at or above the assignment scope first. DoNotEnforce shows impact without blocking, which lets you exempt legitimate resources before switching to Default to enforce deny.

questions.stem: Which standard is assigned by default to Azure subscriptions when you enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
options: Microsoft cloud security benchmark
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark
questions.explain: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) is the default standard. ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-53 and CIS are available regulatory standards that you add explicitly.

questions.case: Litware has Defender for Cloud with only free foundational CSPM on its subscriptions. An auditor asks for a PCI DSS v4 compliance report from the regulatory compliance dashboard. When the admin opens Manage compliance policies, PCI DSS cannot be added.
questions.stem: What must Litware do first?
options: Assign the admin the Security Reader role
Enable a paid Defender plan such as Defender CSPM on the subscriptions
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1
Create a custom initiative with the ASC metadata tag
questions.explain: Adding regulatory standards requires a paid Defender plan other than Defender for Servers Plan 1 or Defender for APIs Plan 1. Security Reader can't add standards, Servers Plan 1 is explicitly not enough, and a custom initiative isn't the PCI DSS standard.

questions.stem: For each statement about the regulatory compliance dashboard in Defender for Cloud, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A greyed-out control is one that cannot be assessed automatically.
You can download audit reports for an assigned standard.
A fully green dashboard for a standard means the organization is certified against that standard.

questions.explain: Greyed-out controls can't be automatically assessed. Audit reports can be downloaded. The dashboard shows automated technical evidence only; certification also requires an auditor's assessment of processes.

questions.stem: You need a custom recommendation in Defender for Cloud that flags VMs without an Owner tag across Azure, AWS and GCP. What should you use?
options: An Azure Policy custom definition added to a custom initiative
A workflow automation that runs a Logic App
A KQL-based custom recommendation with Defender CSPM enabled
A governance rule with a due date
questions.explain: KQL custom recommendations query the cloud security graph across Azure, AWS and GCP and require Defender CSPM. Policy-based custom recommendations work for Azure only; workflow automation and governance rules don't create assessments.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about secure score in Defender for Cloud are true? Select TWO.
options: Recommendations flagged as preview are not included in the score
Remediating higher-risk recommendations improves the score most
Every regulatory standard you add contributes equally to the score
Exempting a resource lowers the score
Secure score is calculated only for AWS accounts
questions.explain: Preview recommendations don't count, and higher-risk open recommendations weigh most. Regulatory standards don't each add to the score, exemptions don't penalise it, and secure score covers Azure, AWS and GCP.

questions.stem: Recommendations keep being remediated late because nobody owns them. You want each recommendation automatically assigned to a resource owner with a due date and email reminders. What should you configure in Defender for Cloud?
options: Continuous export
Alert suppression rules
A security standard
Governance rules
questions.explain: Governance rules assign owners and due dates to recommendations and send notifications. Continuous export streams data elsewhere, suppression rules hide alerts, and a security standard defines what is assessed.

questions.stem: Administrators must still be able to change settings on a production resource group's resources but nobody, including Owners, should be able to delete them without first removing protection. What should you apply?
options: A CanNotDelete lock on the resource group
A ReadOnly lock on the resource group
An Azure Policy with the deny effect
A Reader role assignment for all administrators
questions.explain: CanNotDelete allows read and modify but blocks deletion for everyone. ReadOnly also blocks changes, a deny policy blocks non-compliant creates and updates rather than deletes, and Reader would remove the ability to change settings.

questions.case: An engineer applied a ReadOnly lock to resource group RG-Prod, which contains a storage account, an App Service plan and several VMs. Users report problems the next morning.
questions.stem: Which TWO issues are caused by the lock? Select TWO.
options: Applications using storage account access keys fail because keys can't be listed
VMs in RG-Prod can't be started or restarted
Users can no longer upload blobs with Microsoft Entra credentials
Web apps on the App Service plan stop serving HTTP requests
Users can no longer view the resources in the portal
questions.explain: Listing storage keys and starting VMs are POST control-plane operations blocked by ReadOnly. Blob upload with Entra credentials and serving web traffic are data-plane activity that locks don't affect, and reading resources is still allowed.

questions.stem: You need to prevent accidental deletion of resource group rg-hub while allowing changes to its resources. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code: az lock create --name protect-hub --resource-group rg-hub --lock-type ____
options: ReadOnly
DenyDelete
CanNotDelete
Delete
questions.explain: The CLI lock types are CanNotDelete and ReadOnly. 'Delete' is the portal display name for CanNotDelete, not the CLI value, DenyDelete is a deployment stack deny setting, and ReadOnly would block changes.

questions.stem: A team lead needs to create, update and delete all resources in a resource group, but must not be able to grant access to others. Which built-in role should you assign at the resource group scope?
options: Owner
User Access Administrator
Contributor
Role Based Access Control Administrator
questions.explain: Contributor manages all resources but can't assign roles. Owner and User Access Administrator can grant access, and Role Based Access Control Administrator manages role assignments without managing resources.

questions.case: Contoso wants its platform team lead to assign the Virtual Machine Contributor and Storage Blob Data Reader roles to groups in the Apps subscription. The lead must not be able to assign Owner or any other role, or manage resources.
questions.stem: What should you assign to the lead?
options: Owner on the subscription
User Access Administrator on the subscription
Contributor on the subscription with a NotActions entry
Role Based Access Control Administrator on the subscription with a condition limiting assignable roles
questions.explain: Role Based Access Control Administrator manages only role assignments, and a condition can restrict which roles and principal types the delegate can assign. Owner and User Access Administrator can assign any role; Contributor can't assign roles at all.

questions.stem: You must grant the managed identity of a function app read access to blobs in one storage account only. Complete the command.
questions.code:
az role assignment create \
  --assignee <principal-id> \
  --role "Storage Blob Data Reader" \
  ____ /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-data/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/stdata01
options: --resource-group
--scope
--assignee-object-id
--description
questions.explain: --scope sets the assignment scope by resource ID, here a single storage account. --resource-group would widen the scope to the whole group and takes only a name, --assignee-object-id identifies the principal, and --description is metadata.

questions.stem: You are writing an Azure custom role definition. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An action listed in NotActions is denied even if another role assignment grants it.
A custom role that contains DataActions can be assigned at management group scope.
AssignableScopes can include at most one management group.

questions.explain: NotActions only subtracts from that role's Actions; another assignment can still grant the action. Roles with DataActions can't be assigned at management group scope. A custom role can list only one management group in AssignableScopes.

questions.stem: A DevOps engineer must be able to add and remove client secrets on one specific app registration only, with no other directory permissions. What should you do?
options: Create an Azure custom role with Microsoft.Authorization/* actions and assign it at subscription scope
Create a Microsoft Entra custom role with application credential permissions and assign it scoped to that app registration
Assign the Cloud Application Administrator role at tenant scope
Assign the Application Developer role
questions.explain: Entra custom roles can be scoped to a single app registration and include credential-update permissions. Azure RBAC roles don't manage Entra objects, Cloud Application Administrator covers all apps, and Application Developer only lets users register new apps.

questions.stem: Which licence is required for users who are assigned a Microsoft Entra custom role?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium
questions.explain: Microsoft Entra custom roles require Entra ID P1 for each user with a custom role assignment. Built-in roles are free, P2 is required for PIM rather than custom roles, and Workload ID Premium targets workload identities.

questions.case: An audit of the Finance subscription finds 12 users with permanent Owner, two guest accounts with Contributor that haven't signed in for 120 days, and a service principal with Owner that only ever deploys web apps. Contoso has Entra ID P2 and Defender CSPM.
questions.stem: Which THREE actions best reduce overprivileged access? Select THREE.
options: Convert the users' permanent Owner assignments to PIM eligible assignments
Remove the inactive guest accounts' role assignments
Replace the service principal's Owner role with Website Contributor at the needed scope
Apply a CanNotDelete lock to the subscription
Assign the 12 users Reader in addition to Owner
questions.explain: Making Owner eligible via PIM, removing unused guest access and right-sizing the service principal all reduce privilege. A lock prevents deletion but doesn't remove permissions, and adding Reader doesn't reduce anything because Azure RBAC is additive.

questions.stem: You need Defender for Cloud to identify Azure, AWS and GCP identities whose granted permissions far exceed what they actually use. Which capability provides these recommendations?
options: Cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) in Defender CSPM
Defender for Key Vault
Just-in-time VM access
File integrity monitoring
questions.explain: CIEM, part of Defender CSPM, recommends removing inactive identities and right-sizing overprovisioned ones across Azure, AWS and GCP. Defender for Key Vault detects vault threats, JIT controls VM ports, and file integrity monitoring watches files.

questions.stem: You are setting up a recurring review of who holds Owner on a subscription. Put the steps in order.
options: Open PIM and select the subscription under Azure resources
Create an access review for the Owner role
Choose reviewers, recurrence and auto-apply results settings
Reviewers approve or deny each user's continued access
Denied assignments are removed when results are applied
questions.explain: Access reviews of Azure resource roles are created from PIM for the selected resource; you configure reviewers and settings, reviewers record decisions, and applying the results removes denied access.

questions.stem: A compromised backup administrator account must not be able to disable soft delete or reduce protection on a Recovery Services vault without approval from the security team. Which feature should you implement?
options: Immutable vault in the Enabled state
Cross Region Restore
Multi-user authorization with a Resource Guard
Customer-managed key encryption
questions.explain: Multi-user authorization requires a permission on a separately owned Resource Guard for critical operations such as disabling soft delete. Unlocked immutability can be turned off by the admin, Cross Region Restore is for availability, and CMK covers encryption.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Backup security features, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Locking an immutable vault is irreversible.
The default soft-delete retention for backup data is 90 days.
For multi-user authorization, the backup admin should hold only the Reader role on the Resource Guard.

questions.explain: Locked immutability can't be undone. Azure Backup soft delete defaults to 14 days (configurable to 180); 90 days is Key Vault's default. The backup admin needs only Reader on the Resource Guard, with Backup MUA Operator granted temporarily.

questions.case: A platform team deploys a landing zone's network resources with Bicep from a pipeline that uses a managed identity. Subscription Owners have been editing and deleting the hub resources by hand, causing drift. The team wants Azure to block manual changes and deletions to those resources while the pipeline can still update them.
questions.stem: What should the team use?
options: A deployment stack with deny settings mode denyWriteAndDelete and the pipeline identity as an excluded principal
A CanNotDelete resource lock on the resource group
An Azure Policy assignment with the audit effect
A deployment stack with actionOnUnmanage set to deleteAll
questions.explain: Deployment stack deny settings block writes and deletes for everyone except excluded principals such as the pipeline identity. A CanNotDelete lock still allows edits and also blocks the pipeline from deleting, audit only reports, and actionOnUnmanage controls cleanup, not protection.

questions.stem: An ARM parameter file must take a VM admin password from Key Vault instead of plain text. Complete the parameter.
options: "secretUri"
"secretName"
"keyName"
"value"
questions.explain: A Key Vault reference in a parameter file uses keyVault.id plus secretName (and optionally secretVersion). secretUri is used by App Service Key Vault references, keyName refers to keys, and value would hold a plain-text literal.

questions.stem: Your Azure DevOps pipeline runs the Microsoft Security DevOps extension with the IaC category. Which TWO scanners can analyze your Terraform files? Select TWO.
options: Checkov
Terrascan
Template Analyzer
Bandit
ESLint
questions.explain: Checkov and Terrascan support Terraform. Template Analyzer scans ARM and Bicep templates only, Bandit scans Python code, and ESLint scans JavaScript, so none of them analyze Terraform.

questions.stem: Which storage account setting causes requests sent over plain HTTP to be rejected?
options: Secure transfer required
Minimum TLS version
Allow Blob anonymous access
Allow storage account key access
questions.explain: Secure transfer required accepts only HTTPS (and encrypted SMB). Minimum TLS version rejects old TLS versions but assumes TLS is in use. Anonymous access and key access settings control authorization, not transport.

questions.stem: A container's anonymous access level is set to Container, but the storage account has Allow Blob anonymous access disabled. What happens when an anonymous client tries to list and read the container's blobs?
options: Listing and reading both succeed
Reading blobs succeeds but listing fails
Both succeed only when the client uses TLS 1.2
Both requests fail because the account setting takes precedence
questions.explain: When AllowBlobPublicAccess is false, no container in the account can be accessed anonymously, whatever its own level. Blob-only reads describe the Blob level when the account allows anonymous access. TLS version doesn't affect anonymous authorization.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Storage encryption, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Infrastructure encryption can be enabled on an existing storage account at any time.
A key vault used for storage customer-managed keys must have soft delete and purge protection enabled.
Disabling the customer-managed key in Key Vault causes blob reads and writes to fail with HTTP 403.

questions.explain: Infrastructure encryption is a creation-time choice and can't be changed later. CMK requires soft delete and purge protection on the vault. Disabling the key is the documented way to revoke access, and blob and file data operations then return 403.

questions.stem: You are creating a new storage account and want customer-managed keys configured during creation. Which identity must the account use to access the key vault?
options: A system-assigned managed identity
A user-assigned managed identity
An app registration with a client secret
The storage account access key
questions.explain: A system-assigned identity doesn't exist until the account exists, so CMK at creation time requires a user-assigned managed identity. Existing accounts can use either type. App secrets and account keys aren't used for CMK access.

questions.case: Fabrikam's regulator requires that blob data be encrypted twice with different keys, and that Fabrikam can revoke access to the data by disabling a key it controls. A new storage account will be deployed for this data.
questions.stem: Which two actions should you take? Select TWO.
options: Enable infrastructure encryption when you create the account
Enable encryption at host on the storage account
Configure customer-managed keys from Key Vault for service-level encryption
Regenerate both account access keys every 90 days
Enable Always Encrypted on the blob container
questions.explain: Infrastructure encryption adds a second AES-256 layer and must be set at creation. CMK gives Fabrikam a key it can disable to revoke access. Encryption at host is a VM disk feature, Always Encrypted is for SQL columns, and key rotation doesn't add encryption layers.

questions.stem: Which entry can't be added as an IP network rule in an Azure Storage firewall?
questions.explain: Storage IP network rules accept only public IPv4 addresses and ranges. 10.20.0.0/16 is a private RFC 1918 range; private-network access needs a virtual network rule or a private endpoint. The other entries are public addresses or ranges.

questions.stem: VMs in a subnet in East US must reach a storage account in East US that allows access only from selected networks. Adding the VMs' public IPs to the IP rules didn't help. What should you do?
options: Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on the subnet and add a virtual network rule
Add a resource instance rule for each virtual machine
Select Allow Azure services on the trusted services list to access this storage account
Add the subnet's address range as an IP network rule
questions.explain: IP rules don't apply to same-region clients; a virtual network rule with a service endpoint does. Resource instance rules are for specific service instances such as Synapse workspaces, not VMs. The trusted services exception covers listed Azure services, and private ranges aren't valid IP rules.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Storage network rules, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A resource instance rule can allow a resource that belongs to a different Microsoft Entra tenant.
A client allowed by a network rule still needs valid authorization, such as an RBAC role or a SAS.
A SAS restricted to a specific IP address can grant access from an IP that the storage firewall blocks.

questions.explain: Resource instance rules require the resource to be in the same tenant as the storage account. Network rules only decide who reaches the endpoint; authorization is still required. A SAS IP restriction can only narrow access, never bypass network rules.

questions.stem: You want the storage firewall to deny all traffic except the IP and virtual network rules you add. Complete the Azure CLI command.
questions.code:
az storage account update \
  --name contosodata \
  --resource-group rg-data \
  ____
options: --default-action Deny
--public-network-access Deny
--bypass None
--allow-blob-public-access false
questions.explain: --default-action Deny turns on the firewall so only listed rules are allowed. --public-network-access accepts Enabled or Disabled, not Deny. --bypass controls trusted service exceptions, and --allow-blob-public-access controls anonymous access, not network rules.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Storage feature uses Microsoft Purview sensitive information types to raise the priority of alerts on accounts holding sensitive data?
options: Activity monitoring
Malware scanning
Hash reputation analysis
Sensitive data threat detection
questions.explain: Sensitive data threat detection uses Sensitive Data Discovery and Purview sensitive information types and labels to prioritize alerts. Activity monitoring finds suspicious access, malware scanning checks file content, and hash reputation compares uploads with known malware hashes.

questions.stem: You must ensure that every current and future storage account across 30 subscriptions is protected by Defender for Storage with minimal ongoing effort. What should you do?
options: Enable Defender for Storage on each storage account as it is created
Enable resource logs on every account and connect them to Microsoft Sentinel
Enable the Defender CSPM plan on each subscription
Assign the built-in Azure Policy that enables Defender for Storage at subscription level
questions.explain: Subscription-level enablement covers new accounts automatically, and Azure Policy enforces it across many subscriptions and prevents drift. Per-account enablement misses new accounts. Defender for Storage doesn't need resource logs, and Defender CSPM is a posture plan, not storage threat protection.

questions.stem: Which two can Defender for Storage malware scanning scan? Select TWO.
options: Block blobs in a Data Lake Storage Gen2 (hierarchical namespace) account
Blobs uploaded over NFS 3.0
Blobs encrypted client-side before upload
Block blobs in a general-purpose v2 account
Append blobs used for log files
questions.explain: Malware scanning supports block blobs in GPv2 and hierarchical namespace accounts. Append and page blobs, NFS 3.0 uploads, and client-side encrypted blobs aren't supported (server-side CMK encryption is fine).

questions.stem: Malicious files found by malware scanning must be removed from applications' view automatically but remain recoverable for a period, without writing custom code. Which option should you configure?
options: An ABAC condition based on the scan result index tag
Enable blob versioning on the storage account
A time-based immutability policy on the container
Soft delete malicious blobs in the Defender for Storage settings
questions.explain: The built-in soft delete malicious blobs option soft-deletes flagged blobs, enabling blob soft delete if needed, so they can be restored within retention. ABAC blocks access but doesn't remove files. Versioning keeps copies but doesn't remove the current malicious blob, and immutability prevents deletion.

questions.stem: What is the default monthly malware scanning cap per storage account in Defender for Storage?
options: Unlimited
questions.explain: The default cap is 10,000 GB scanned per storage account per month. It can be changed at subscription or account level, and alerts fire at 75% and when scanning pauses. It isn't unlimited by default.

questions.stem: Malware scan results are sent to a Log Analytics workspace. Complete the KQL query to list malicious files.
questions.code:
____
| where ScanResultType == "Malicious"
| project TimeGenerated, StorageAccountName, ScannedObjectUri
options: StorageBlobLogs
StorageMalwareScanningResults
SecurityAlert
AzureDiagnostics
questions.explain: StorageMalwareScanningResults holds every scan result with ScanResultType, StorageAccountName and ScannedObjectUri. StorageBlobLogs holds request logs, SecurityAlert holds alerts with a different schema, and AzureDiagnostics is the legacy shared table.

questions.case: Contoso's claims app stores customer uploads in a storage account with on-upload malware scanning. Within seconds of each scan, clean files must be copied to a processing container and malicious files moved to a quarantine account.
questions.stem: Which approach should you use?
options: Send scan results to an Event Grid custom topic and trigger an Azure Function
Trigger a Logic App from Defender for Cloud security alerts
Query StorageMalwareScanningResults every hour with a scheduled job
Read the blob index tags with a nightly script
questions.explain: Event Grid delivers every scan result, clean or malicious, in near real time, so a Function can route both. Security alerts only fire for malicious files, so they can't forward clean files. Hourly queries and nightly scripts miss the seconds-level requirement.

questions.stem: Which type of shared access signature is signed with credentials obtained through Microsoft Entra ID?
options: Account SAS
Service SAS
Ad hoc SAS
User delegation SAS
questions.explain: A user delegation SAS is signed with a user delegation key requested with Entra credentials. Account and service SASs are signed with the account key. Ad hoc SAS describes a key-signed SAS that isn't linked to a stored access policy.

questions.stem: A partner holds several service SAS tokens that reference a stored access policy on a container. You must revoke them all without regenerating the account keys. What should you do?
options: Revoke all user delegation keys for the account
Delete the stored access policy or set its expiry to a past time
Set the account's SAS expiration policy action to Block
Change the container's anonymous access level to Private
questions.explain: Service SASs linked to a stored access policy become invalid when the policy is deleted, renamed or expired. Revoking user delegation keys affects only user delegation SASs. A SAS expiration policy only checks new requests against a maximum lifetime, and anonymous access level is unrelated to SAS.

questions.stem: For each statement about SAS and stored access policies, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A user delegation SAS can be associated with a stored access policy.
A blob container can have up to five stored access policies at the same time.
A user delegation SAS can be valid for at most seven days.

questions.explain: Stored access policies work only with service SAS. The limit is five policies per container, queue, table or share. The user delegation key, and therefore the SAS, is limited to seven days.

questions.case: Security policy at Northwind says no SAS may be valid for more than 8 hours. Requests using longer-lived tokens must be refused, and the team wants a report of which accounts received such requests.
questions.stem: Which two actions should you take? Select TWO.
options: Configure a SAS expiration policy of 8 hours with the action set to Log
Enable Defender for Storage activity monitoring
Create a stored access policy with an 8-hour expiry on every container
Send blob logs to Log Analytics and query StorageBlobLogs for SasExpiryStatus
Configure a SAS expiration policy of 8 hours with the action set to Block
questions.explain: Block refuses out-of-policy SAS requests, and violations are recorded in the SasExpiryStatus field of StorageBlobLogs. Log only records violations without refusing them. Stored access policies only govern service SASs that reference them, and Defender doesn't enforce SAS lifetimes.

questions.stem: All clients now use Microsoft Entra ID. Complete the Azure CLI command to block requests authorized with the account keys.
questions.code:
az storage account update \
  --name contosodata \
  --resource-group rg-data \
  ____
options: --allow-shared-key-access false
--https-only true
--allow-blob-public-access false
--default-action Deny
questions.explain: --allow-shared-key-access false sets AllowSharedKeyAccess so key-signed requests, account SAS and service SAS get 403. The other parameters control anonymous access, HTTPS enforcement and the network firewall.

questions.stem: You plan to disable Shared Key authorization across storage accounts without breaking applications. Put the steps in order.
options: Assign the policy Storage accounts should prevent shared key access in Audit mode
Identify clients using account keys or SAS with the Transactions metric or StorageBlobLogs
Migrate those clients to Microsoft Entra ID or user delegation SAS
Set AllowSharedKeyAccess to false on the accounts
Change the policy assignment effect from Audit to Deny
questions.explain: Audit first to find non-compliant accounts, then find and migrate the clients that still use keys. Only then disable Shared Key, and finally switch the policy to Deny so new accounts can't re-enable it.

questions.stem: A user must read blobs in one container using Microsoft Entra ID and must not be able to manage the storage account or read its keys. Which role should you assign at the container scope?
options: Reader
Storage Account Contributor
Storage Blob Delegator
Storage Blob Data Reader
questions.explain: Storage Blob Data Reader grants data plane read access with Entra tokens. Reader is a control plane role that can't read blob data. Storage Account Contributor can list keys and manage the account. Storage Blob Delegator only allows getting a user delegation key.

questions.stem: What is the effect of enabling Allow Azure services and resources to access this server on an Azure SQL logical server?
options: Only resources in your own subscription can connect
Connections from any Azure resource, including other customers' subscriptions, pass the firewall
Only Azure services on the trusted services list can connect with managed identities
Public network access is disabled and private endpoints are required
questions.explain: The setting adds a 0.0.0.0 server rule that admits all traffic from Azure, including resources outside your subscription, which is why Microsoft calls it more permissive than most customers want. It isn't scoped to your subscription, isn't a trusted-services list, and doesn't disable public access.

questions.stem: You need an IP firewall rule that applies only to the SalesDB database, not other databases on the server. While connected to SalesDB, complete the T-SQL.
options: sp_set_firewall_rule
sp_set_database_firewall_rule
sp_add_firewall_rule
sp_set_db_network_rule
questions.explain: sp_set_database_firewall_rule creates a database-level rule, the only way to create one. sp_set_firewall_rule creates a server-level rule in master that covers every database. The other procedure names don't exist.

questions.stem: An administrator tries to add a server-level IP firewall rule to an Azure SQL logical server and receives an error that firewall rules can't be modified. What is the most likely cause?
options: Public network access is set to Disable
Microsoft Entra-only authentication is enabled
The connection policy is set to Redirect
The minimum TLS version is set to 1.2
questions.explain: When public network access is disabled, only private endpoints are allowed and creating or editing IP or virtual network firewall rules is refused. Entra-only authentication, connection policy and TLS version don't block firewall rule changes.

questions.stem: A security engineer must be able to enable or disable Microsoft Entra-only authentication on Azure SQL servers without getting broad rights to manage the servers. Which built-in role should you assign?
options: SQL Server Contributor
SQL DB Contributor
SQL Security Manager
Security Reader
questions.explain: SQL Security Manager includes the azureADOnlyAuthentications actions. SQL Server Contributor and SQL Managed Instance Contributor deliberately can't change this setting, for separation of duties. SQL DB Contributor manages databases, and Security Reader is read-only.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra-only authentication for Azure SQL, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Enabling it deletes the existing SQL authentication logins.
A Microsoft Entra admin must be set on the server before it can be enabled.
It is also supported on Azure SQL Managed Instance.

questions.explain: SQL logins remain but can't connect while the setting is on. Enabling fails if no Entra admin is configured. Managed Instance supports it too, with az sql mi ad-only-auth commands.

questions.stem: Complete the Azure CLI command that blocks SQL authentication on the logical server sql-prod.
questions.code:
az sql server ____ enable \
  --resource-group rg-sql \
  --name sql-prod
options: ad-admin
audit-policy
firewall-rule
ad-only-auth
questions.explain: az sql server ad-only-auth enable turns on Microsoft Entra-only authentication. ad-admin sets the Entra admin (a prerequisite), audit-policy configures auditing, and firewall-rule manages IP rules; none has an enable subcommand that blocks SQL logins.

questions.stem: How is a newly created Azure SQL Database encrypted at rest by default?
options: It isn't encrypted until you enable TDE
Always Encrypted with keys stored in Key Vault
TDE with a customer-managed key in Key Vault
Transparent data encryption with a service-managed key
questions.explain: New databases have TDE on by default with a service-managed TDE protector (AES-256). Customer-managed keys are optional. Always Encrypted is a separate column-level feature you configure yourself.

questions.case: A health insurer stores national ID numbers in Azure SQL Database. Database administrators must not be able to see the plaintext values, but the claims application must still look up customers by exact national ID.
questions.stem: What should you implement for the national ID column?
options: TDE with a customer-managed TDE protector
Always Encrypted with deterministic encryption
Always Encrypted with randomized encryption and no secure enclave
Dynamic data masking
questions.explain: Always Encrypted keeps plaintext away from the engine and DBAs; deterministic encryption allows equality lookups. TDE only protects data at rest, so DBAs still see values. Randomized encryption without an enclave can't support lookups. Dynamic data masking can be bypassed by privileged users.

questions.stem: You will configure a customer-managed TDE protector for an Azure SQL logical server. Which three requirements must be met? Select THREE.
options: The server's managed identity has get, wrapKey and unwrapKey permissions on the key
Always Encrypted is enabled on the database first
Soft delete and purge protection are enabled on the key vault
The key is an asymmetric RSA or RSA-HSM key
The key is a symmetric AES-256 key
questions.explain: TDE BYOK needs a vault with soft delete and purge protection, an asymmetric RSA key, and server identity permissions to get, wrap and unwrap. The TDE protector isn't a symmetric key, and Always Encrypted is unrelated.

questions.stem: Auditing is enabled on an Azure SQL logical server, and a database on that server also has its own database-level audit policy enabled. What happens?
options: The database policy overrides the server policy for that database
The server policy overrides the database policy
Both audits run side by side, so the database is audited twice
Saving the database policy fails while server auditing is on
questions.explain: In Azure SQL Database the database audit exists side by side with the server audit, so both capture events. Neither overrides the other, and there is no conflict error. Usually you enable one level unless you need different destinations.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure SQL Database auditing, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A retention value of 0 for storage audit logs means unlimited retention.
Choosing Log Analytics as a destination creates a diagnostic setting with the SQLSecurityAuditEvents category.
Audit logs written to Azure Storage are stored as JSON files in block blobs.

questions.explain: Retention defaults to 0, meaning logs are kept indefinitely. Log Analytics and Event Hubs destinations work through a SQLSecurityAuditEvents diagnostic setting. Storage audit logs are .xel files in append blobs.

questions.case: Server-level auditing for an Azure SQL server must write to a storage account that allows access only from selected networks and has Allow storage account key access disabled.
questions.stem: Which three actions should you take? Select THREE.
options: Configure auditing to authenticate to storage with a managed identity
Assign the server's identity the Storage Blob Data Contributor role on the storage account
Create a stored access policy on the audit container
Configure auditing to use the storage access key
Allow trusted Microsoft services to access the storage account
questions.explain: With key access disabled, auditing must use managed identity, which needs Storage Blob Data Contributor, and the firewall must allow trusted Microsoft services. Storage keys are blocked, and stored access policies apply to service SAS, which auditing doesn't use.

questions.stem: You are configuring auditing on Azure SQL Managed Instance to a blob container. Put the steps in order.
options: CREATE CREDENTIAL named with the container URL, using a SAS as the secret
CREATE SERVER AUDIT ... TO URL pointing at the container
CREATE SERVER AUDIT SPECIFICATION with the required action groups
ALTER SERVER AUDIT ... WITH (STATE = ON)
questions.explain: The audit needs a credential to write to the container, so create it first. Then define the audit and its target, then the specification that says what to capture, and finally turn the audit on.

questions.stem: A diagnostic setting on Azure SQL Managed Instance sends SQLSecurityAuditEvents to Log Analytics. Complete the T-SQL so that audit events use that path.
questions.code:
CREATE SERVER AUDIT [SocAudit] TO ____;
GO
options: FILE
URL
EXTERNAL_MONITOR
APPLICATION_LOG
questions.explain: TO EXTERNAL_MONITOR sends audit events through diagnostic settings to Log Analytics or Event Hubs. TO URL writes to blob storage. FILE and APPLICATION_LOG are SQL Server audit targets that don't apply to this scenario.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Azure SQL capability reports misconfigurations such as excessive permissions and lets you approve a baseline of accepted results?
options: SQL vulnerability assessment
Advanced Threat Protection
Data Discovery & Classification
Azure SQL auditing
questions.explain: SQL vulnerability assessment scans for misconfigurations and supports baselines. Advanced Threat Protection detects attacks such as SQL injection. Data Discovery & Classification labels sensitive columns, and auditing records events.

questions.stem: You want SQL vulnerability assessment on Azure SQL Database without creating or managing a storage account for scan results, and baselines should apply without a rescan. Which option should you use?
options: Classic configuration with a storage account
Server-level auditing to Log Analytics
Express configuration
Microsoft Purview data map scanning
questions.explain: Express configuration stores results in Defender for Cloud-managed storage and applies baselines without rescanning. Classic configuration needs your own storage account and a rescan. Auditing and Purview scanning don't perform vulnerability assessment.

questions.stem: Which three plan components are turned on when you set the Databases plan to On in Defender for Cloud? Select THREE.
options: Defender for Key Vault
Defender for Azure SQL Databases
Defender for Storage
Defender for Open-Source Relational Databases
Defender for Azure Cosmos DB
questions.explain: The Databases plan covers Azure SQL Databases, SQL Servers on Machines, Open-Source Relational Databases and Azure Cosmos DB. Defender for Storage and Defender for Key Vault are separate Defender for Cloud plans.

questions.stem: An NSG has an inbound rule at priority 200 that denies TCP 3389 from Internet and a rule at priority 300 that allows TCP 3389 from Internet. What happens to an inbound RDP connection from the internet?
options: It is denied because priority 200 is processed first
It is allowed because Allow rules take precedence
It is allowed because the higher number has higher priority
It is denied by the default DenyAllInbound rule only
questions.explain: NSG rules are processed from the lowest priority number, and processing stops at the first match, so the Deny at 200 wins. Allow rules have no special precedence, and the default rule at 65500 is never reached because a custom rule matched.

questions.stem: A VM has an NSG on its subnet that allows inbound TCP 443 and an NSG on its NIC that has only the default rules. Can clients on the internet reach the VM on 443?
options: Yes, because the subnet NSG is evaluated last for inbound traffic
Yes, because NIC NSGs with only default rules are ignored
No, because the NIC NSG's DenyAllInbound rule blocks the traffic
No, because subnet NSGs can't allow traffic from the internet
questions.explain: Inbound traffic passes the subnet NSG and then the NIC NSG; both must allow it. The NIC NSG's DenyAllInbound default rule blocks internet traffic. NSGs with default rules are not ignored, and subnet NSGs can allow internet traffic.

questions.stem: For each statement about network security groups, select Yes if true.

statements.s: You can delete the AllowInternetOutBound default rule to block internet access.
Return traffic for an allowed inbound connection is allowed without an outbound rule.
Custom NSG rules can use priorities from 100 to 4096.

questions.explain: Default rules can't be deleted, only overridden by a higher-priority rule such as Deny Internet at 4000. NSGs are stateful, so replies are allowed. Custom rule priority ranges from 100 to 4096.

questions.stem: You must allow outbound traffic from a subnet to Azure Storage in West Europe only, without maintaining IP address lists as Azure changes them. What should you use as the NSG rule's destination?
options: An application security group containing the storage account
The Internet service tag
The Storage.WestEurope service tag
The VirtualNetwork service tag
questions.explain: Regional service tags such as Storage.WestEurope are maintained by Microsoft and cover that service's prefixes in the region. ASGs contain NICs, not PaaS services. Internet is far too broad, and VirtualNetwork covers your own address space.

questions.stem: NSG flow logs are being retired. Which Network Watcher feature should you use to log IP traffic flows for new deployments?
options: Connection monitor
Virtual network flow logs
Packet capture
Azure Monitor activity log
questions.explain: Virtual network flow logs replace NSG flow logs and work with Traffic analytics. Connection monitor tracks reachability over time, packet capture records full packets for a session, and the activity log records control plane operations, not traffic flows.

questions.stem: Web servers scale in and out frequently, and their IP addresses change. You need an NSG rule allowing only web servers to reach database servers on TCP 1433. What should you use as source and destination?
options: Service tags for the web and database tiers
