questions.stem: A new Azure WAF policy must log matched attacks without blocking traffic while you tune false positives. Which mode should you use?
options: Prevention
Detection
Audit
Anomaly
questions.explain: Detection mode logs matches and lets the requests through, which is the recommended starting point. Prevention blocks. 'Audit' isn't a WAF mode, and anomaly scoring is a rule action, not a mode.

questions.stem: You need managed OWASP rule sets and bot protection at Microsoft's global edge for a website. Which service should you deploy?
options: Azure Front Door Standard with a WAF policy
Azure Firewall Premium
Application Gateway WAF_v2 in a single region
Azure Front Door Premium with a WAF policy
questions.explain: Front Door Premium supports managed rule sets and bot protection at the global edge. Front Door Standard supports custom rules only. Application Gateway is regional, not edge. Azure Firewall Premium is a network firewall with IDPS, not a web application firewall.

questions.stem: A WAF policy on Application Gateway uses DRS with anomaly scoring in Prevention mode. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A request that matches a single Critical-severity rule is blocked.
A request that matches a single Warning-severity rule is blocked.
Custom rules are evaluated before the managed rule set.

questions.explain: Critical adds 5 points, which reaches the threshold of 5 and blocks the request. Warning adds only 3. Custom rules are always processed before managed rules.

questions.stem: API Management must reject calls that don't carry a valid Microsoft Entra access token for the Orders API. Complete the inbound policy.
questions.code:
<inbound>
  <base />
  <____ header-name="Authorization" failed-validation-httpcode="401">
    <openid-config url="https://login.microsoftonline.com/contoso.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration" />
    <audiences>
      <audience>api://orders</audience>
    </audiences>
  </validate-jwt>
</inbound>
options: validate-jwt
check-header
authentication-managed-identity
validate-client-certificate
questions.explain: validate-jwt checks the token's signature against the OpenID configuration, along with its audience and claims. check-header only confirms a header exists. authentication-managed-identity authenticates APIM to the back end. validate-client-certificate checks mTLS certificates, not JWTs.

questions.stem: API Management must call a back-end Azure Function using a Microsoft Entra token, without storing a client secret in APIM. Which policy should you add to the inbound section?
options: authentication-basic
set-backend-service
authentication-managed-identity
rate-limit-by-key
questions.explain: authentication-managed-identity gets an Entra token with APIM's managed identity for the back end's resource. Basic authentication sends stored credentials. set-backend-service changes the routing URL. rate-limit-by-key throttles calls.

questions.case: Contoso publishes an internal back-end API through API Management with validate-jwt and rate-limit-by-key policies. A test shows callers can still reach the back end directly at its public App Service URL, bypassing every APIM policy.
questions.stem: What should you do to make sure all traffic goes through API Management?
options: Add an ip-filter policy in APIM
Increase the rate-limit-by-key threshold
Require a subscription key on the API
Restrict the back end to accept traffic only from APIM, using a private endpoint or access restrictions
questions.explain: APIM policies only apply to traffic that passes through APIM, so the back end has to be locked down to accept only APIM. Policies in APIM, such as ip-filter, rate limits or subscription keys, can't affect direct calls to the back end.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud capability requires the paid Defender CSPM plan?
options: Attack path analysis
Secure score
Security recommendations based on the Microsoft cloud security benchmark
Asset inventory
questions.explain: Attack path analysis is a Defender CSPM feature built on the cloud security graph. Secure score, the MCSB recommendations and asset inventory all come with free Foundational CSPM.

questions.stem: A security engineer wants to search proactively for internet-exposed VMs that have high-severity vulnerabilities and permissions to reach storage accounts holding sensitive data. What should the engineer use?
options: The Regulatory compliance dashboard
Cloud security explorer in Defender CSPM
Workflow automation in Defender for Cloud
Secure score recommendations grouped by control
questions.explain: Cloud security explorer runs graph queries that combine exposure, vulnerabilities and access paths. The compliance dashboard shows control status, workflow automation runs Logic Apps on events, and secure score controls don't correlate resources with each other.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Attack path analysis requires Defender CSPM with agentless scanning turned on.
Secure score is only available after you enable the Defender CSPM plan.
After you remediate an attack path, it can take up to 24 hours to disappear from the list.

questions.explain: Attack paths need Defender CSPM and agentless scanning. Secure score is part of free Foundational CSPM. Resolved paths can stay listed for up to 24 hours.

questions.stem: An administrator must add the PCI DSS v4.0.1 standard to a subscription in Defender for Cloud. Which two Azure roles allow this? Select TWO.
options: Owner
Security Reader
Policy Contributor
Log Analytics Contributor
Reader
questions.explain: To add a regulatory standard you need Owner or Policy Contributor, because standards are Azure Policy initiatives. Security Reader and Reader can only view, and Log Analytics Contributor manages workspaces, not policy.

questions.stem: A subscription has only Defender for Servers Plan 1 enabled. An auditor asks you to add ISO/IEC 27001:2022 to the Regulatory compliance dashboard, but the standard can't be assigned. What should you do first?
options: Assign the Security Reader role to the auditor
Enable Foundational CSPM on the subscription
Enable the Defender CSPM plan on the subscription
Upgrade the tenant to Microsoft Entra ID P2
questions.explain: Extra standards need a Defender plan other than Servers Plan 1 or APIs Plan 1, and Defender CSPM is the usual choice. Foundational CSPM is already on and free. The other two changes have no effect on standards.

questions.stem: Which security standard does Defender for Cloud assign by default to Azure subscriptions?
options: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
Microsoft cloud security benchmark
questions.explain: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) is the default for Azure, and it's also applied to AWS and GCP. The others are optional standards you add yourself.

questions.stem: You need to add a regulatory compliance standard in Defender for Cloud. Put the steps in order.
options: Open Microsoft Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance
Select Manage compliance policies
Select the subscription, management group, AWS account or GCP project
Select Security policies
Set the standard's status to On and provide any parameters
questions.explain: Go from Regulatory compliance to Manage compliance policies, pick the scope, open Security policies, then turn the standard on. Some standards then ask for parameters.

questions.stem: Customers upload files to an Azure Blob Storage account. You need every uploaded blob scanned for malware. Which plan should you enable?
options: Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager
Microsoft Defender for Key Vault
Microsoft Defender for Storage
Defender CSPM
questions.explain: Malware scanning on upload is a Defender for Storage feature that uses the Microsoft Defender Antivirus engine. Resource Manager watches control-plane operations, Key Vault watches secret access, and CSPM covers posture rather than content scanning.

questions.stem: You need alerts when someone runs unusual Azure management operations, such as mass deployments from an unfamiliar IP address, against your subscriptions. Which plan should you enable?
options: Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager
Microsoft Defender for APIs
Microsoft Defender for App Service
Microsoft Defender for Key Vault
questions.explain: Defender for Resource Manager monitors Azure control-plane (ARM) operations for suspicious activity. Defender for APIs protects published APIs, App Service protects web apps, and Key Vault protects vault access.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: By default, Defender for Storage malware scanning has a cap of 10,000 GB scanned per storage account per month.
Defender for Storage requires an agent installed on a VM next to the storage account.
Azure Policy for Kubernetes is a component of Defender for Containers.

questions.explain: The default malware-scanning cap is 10,000 GB per account per month. Defender for Storage is agentless. Defender for Containers uses the Defender sensor and Azure Policy for Kubernetes.

questions.case: Fabrikam runs 300 Azure VMs in one subscription. Security wants RDP and SSH ports closed unless an admin requests time-limited access. Changes to critical system files must be tracked, and vulnerabilities must be found even on VMs where the Defender for Endpoint sensor isn't healthy.
questions.stem: Which Defender for Servers configuration meets the requirements?
options: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 on the subscription
Enable Defender CSPM on the subscription
Enable Plan 1 and turn on Foundational CSPM recommendations
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 on the subscription
questions.explain: Just-in-time VM access, file integrity monitoring and agentless scanning are all Plan 2 features. Plan 1 gives EDR through Defender for Endpoint and agent-based vulnerability management. Defender CSPM has agentless scanning but not JIT or FIM.

questions.stem: A subscription holds 200 VMs. Only 10 of them need Defender for Endpoint EDR protection, and you must keep cost as low as possible. What should you do?
options: Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 at resource level on the 10 VMs
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 at resource level on the 10 VMs
Enable Defender CSPM on the 10 VMs only
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 1 on the management group
questions.explain: Plan 1 can be enabled per resource and includes Defender for Endpoint integration. Plan 2 can't be enabled per resource. Defender CSPM doesn't provide EDR, and a management group assignment would cover all 200 VMs.

questions.stem: Which three capabilities are included in Defender for Servers Plan 2 but not Plan 1? Select THREE.
options: 500 MB of free daily data ingestion
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration
Agent-based vulnerability scanning with Defender Vulnerability Management
Agentless vulnerability scanning
Just-in-time VM access
questions.explain: Agentless scanning, JIT VM access and the 500 MB daily ingestion benefit are Plan 2 only. Both plans include Defender for Endpoint integration and agent-based MDVM scanning.

questions.stem: Your company uses AWS Organizations with 60 member accounts, and new accounts are created every month. Every account, including future ones, must appear in Defender for Cloud with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
options: Create a single-account connector for each member account by using IAM access keys
Onboard the AWS management account and deploy the CloudFormation StackSet
Delegate the AWS accounts with Azure Lighthouse
Connect each account by using the Microsoft Sentinel Amazon Web Services S3 connector
questions.explain: Onboarding the management account auto-provisions connectors for current and new member accounts through StackSets. The connectors use federated trust instead of access keys. Lighthouse manages Azure tenants, and the Sentinel S3 connector only ingests logs.

questions.stem: How does the Defender for Cloud GCP connector authenticate to Google Cloud?
options: A service account JSON key stored in Azure Key Vault
An OAuth consent grant to a multitenant Microsoft Entra app
The Azure Arc Connected Machine agent on each GCP instance
Workload identity federation with service account impersonation, created by the generated gcloud script
questions.explain: The onboarding script creates a workload identity pool, providers and service accounts, so Defender for Cloud never stores long-lived keys. Azure Arc onboards servers, but that isn't how the connector authenticates.

questions.stem: You are connecting an AWS account to Defender for Cloud in the Azure portal. Put the steps in order.
options: Go to Environment settings > Add environment > Amazon Web Services
Enter the connector name, AWS account ID, regions and scan interval
Select the Defender plans to enable
Configure access by choosing a permissions type and a deployment method
Select Review and generate, then select Create
questions.explain: The wizard runs from account details to plan selection to access configuration (CloudFormation or Terraform), and ends with review and create.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A scan interval of 4 hours can be selected for an AWS connector.
The AWS connector stores long-lived AWS access keys in Defender for Cloud.
On-premises servers are protected by Defender for Servers after onboarding to Azure Arc.

questions.explain: AWS scan intervals are 4, 6, 12 or 24 hours. The connector uses federated trust and short-lived credentials. Azure Arc brings on-premises servers under Defender for Servers.

questions.stem: Where do you turn on Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management as the vulnerability assessment solution for Azure VMs?
options: Defender for Cloud > Environment settings > subscription > Defender for Servers settings > Vulnerability assessment for machines
Defender portal > Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features > Microsoft Intune connection
Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance > Manage compliance policies
Azure Policy > Assign the 'Deploy Log Analytics agent' initiative
questions.explain: Vulnerability assessment for machines is a component setting of the Defender for Servers plan in Environment settings. The Intune connection, compliance policies and the retired Log Analytics agent don't configure MDVM.

questions.stem: Several Azure VMs have no Defender for Endpoint sensor, and policy forbids installing new software on them. You still need vulnerability findings. What should you enable?
options: File integrity monitoring
Just-in-time VM access
Agentless scanning for machines, with Defender for Servers Plan 2 or Defender CSPM
The Azure Monitor Agent with a Windows Security Events DCR
questions.explain: Agentless scanning reads a disk snapshot and needs nothing installed on the VM. FIM tracks file changes and JIT controls ports, and neither finds CVEs. AMA is an agent and collects logs, not vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Agent-based vulnerability scanning with Defender Vulnerability Management is available with Defender for Servers Plan 1.
For agentless scanning, disk snapshots are copied to another Azure region for analysis.
Agentless scanning of disks encrypted with customer-managed keys requires extra Key Vault key permissions.

questions.explain: Both plans include agent-based MDVM scanning. The snapshot stays in the VM's region and is deleted after analysis. CMK disks need key read, wrap and unwrap permissions.

questions.stem: Which of these can't be used as a discovery seed in Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management?
options: The private address range 10.0.0.0/8
The domain contoso.com
An autonomous system number (ASN)
A Whois organization name
questions.explain: Defender EASM works from the outside in, so private IP addresses aren't accepted as seeds. Domains, ASNs, Whois organizations, hosts, IP blocks and email contacts are all valid seeds.

questions.stem: Your company already pays for Defender CSPM. You want attack paths that start from internet-exposed IP addresses, without extra licensing. What should you do?
options: Buy a standalone Defender EASM resource and link it to each subscription
Use the Defender EASM integration that Defender CSPM already includes
Enable Defender for APIs on every subscription
Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 on every subscription
questions.explain: Defender CSPM includes the EASM integration for internet-exposure validation, attack paths and explorer queries, and it doesn't need a separate EASM licence. A standalone EASM resource is only needed to work with EASM inventory directly.

questions.stem: Which two dashboards are available in Defender EASM? Select TWO.
options: MITRE ATT&CK coverage
Attack path analysis
Secure score over time
CISA known exploits
OWASP Top 10
questions.explain: Defender EASM dashboards include Overview, Inventory changes, Attack surface summary, Security posture, GDPR compliance, OWASP Top 10, CWE top 25 and CISA known exploits. Attack paths and secure score belong to Defender for Cloud.

questions.stem: Two Microsoft Sentinel workspaces are onboarded to the Defender portal. Defender XDR incidents are correlated with Sentinel alerts for WS-EU but not for WS-US. What is the most likely reason?
options: WS-US analysts need the Microsoft Sentinel Responder role
WS-US must first be migrated to the Sentinel data lake tier
WS-EU is the primary workspace, and only the primary workspace receives the Defender XDR connector
Defender XDR incidents are routed by Azure region
questions.explain: In the Defender portal, one primary workspace per tenant gets the Defender XDR connector and unified incidents. Secondary workspaces can ingest Defender tables but don't get XDR incidents. Roles and regions don't change this.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: After deployment, a Microsoft Sentinel workspace can be moved to another resource group.
The Defender portal supports one primary workspace and multiple secondary workspaces per tenant.
When you change the primary workspace, the Defender XDR connector moves to the new primary automatically.

questions.explain: Sentinel doesn't support moving the workspace after deployment. The Defender portal allows one primary and unlimited secondary workspaces, and changing the primary moves the XDR connector automatically.

questions.stem: Hunters must query sign-ins from the current workspace and from the contoso-eu workspace in one query. Complete the query.
questions.code:
union SigninLogs, ____("contoso-eu").SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize count() by UserPrincipalName
options: app
cluster
database
workspace
questions.explain: workspace() references a table in another Log Analytics workspace. app() targets Application Insights, while cluster() and database() target Azure Data Explorer.

questions.stem: Tier-1 analysts must assign incidents and change their status. They must not create analytics rules. Which role should you assign?
options: Microsoft Sentinel Reader
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Responder
Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor
questions.explain: Responder adds incident management to Reader permissions. Reader can't change incidents, Contributor can also create rules, and Automation Contributor is a service role, not one for analysts.

questions.stem: An analyst must be able to list and manually run existing playbooks but not edit them. Which role meets this requirement with the least privilege?
options: Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
Logic App Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
questions.explain: Playbook Operator lets a user list, view and manually run playbooks. Logic App Contributor can also edit them. Automation Contributor is for the Sentinel service, and Sentinel Contributor grants far more than needed.

questions.case: A detection engineer at Contoso must create and tune analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel. They must also build and edit the Logic Apps playbooks that run when incidents are created. All Sentinel resources are in the RG-SOC resource group. Assign the fewest roles that meet the requirements.
questions.stem: Which two roles should you assign to the detection engineer? Select TWO.
options: Logic App Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Responder
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
questions.explain: Sentinel Contributor allows creating analytics rules and installing content. Playbooks are Logic Apps, so editing them needs Logic App Contributor. Playbook Operator only runs them, Responder only manages incidents, and Automation Contributor is for the service.

questions.stem: You installed the Microsoft Entra ID solution from the content hub and connected its data connector. Two days later, no incidents have been created from Entra ID data. What should you do?
options: Wait for the solution's rules to be enabled automatically after 72 hours
Assign the Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor role to the SOC
Reinstall the solution as standalone content
Create analytics rules from the solution's rule templates
questions.explain: Installing a solution only deploys templates. You must create active analytics rules from them before any detections run. Rules are never enabled automatically, and roles or reinstalling won't create them.

questions.stem: You need to deploy detections from a content hub solution. Put the steps in order.
options: Open Content hub and find the solution
Select Install (or Install with dependencies)
Select Manage on the installed solution
Select an analytics rule template and choose Create rule
Complete the rule wizard and save the rule as enabled
questions.explain: Install the solution, use Manage to see its content, then create and save rules from the templates. Until you do that, the content is only templates.

questions.stem: You enabled the Microsoft Entra ID connector, but the SigninLogs table stays empty while AuditLogs fills normally. The tenant has only Microsoft Entra ID Free. What is the cause?
options: The Azure Monitor Agent isn't installed on a domain controller
Sign-in logs require a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licence
The connector needs a data collection endpoint
Sign-in logs are only sent to the AADProvisioningLogs table
questions.explain: Exporting sign-in logs needs Entra ID P1 or P2. Audit logs work with any licence. The connector is API-based, so it needs no agent or DCE, and sign-ins go to SigninLogs.

questions.stem: You assigned the Azure Policy for a diagnostic settings-based Sentinel connector. New Key Vaults now send logs, but existing Key Vaults don't. What should you have done?
options: Assigned the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role to every Key Vault
Selected Create a remediation task in the policy assignment
Installed the Azure Monitor Agent on each Key Vault
Configured a Logs Ingestion API DCR for the Key Vaults
questions.explain: A policy assignment by itself only applies to new or updated resources. A remediation task applies the diagnostic setting to resources that already exist. Key Vault has no agent, and the Logs Ingestion API isn't used for this.

questions.stem: You enable the Microsoft Entra ID connector with Sign-in logs and Non-interactive user sign-in logs selected. Which two tables will receive data? Select TWO.
options: SigninLogs
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
AzureActivity
SecurityEvent
IdentityLogonEvents
questions.explain: Interactive sign-ins go to SigninLogs and non-interactive ones go to AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs. IdentityLogonEvents is a Defender XDR table, SecurityEvent holds Windows events, and AzureActivity holds Azure control-plane events.

questions.stem: You need a list of role assignment writes from the Azure Activity connector that shows only the time, caller and resource group. Complete the query.
questions.code:
AzureActivity
| where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/ROLEASSIGNMENTS/WRITE"
| ____ TimeGenerated, Caller, ResourceGroup
options: extend
summarize
render
project
questions.explain: project returns only the listed columns. extend adds columns and keeps all the others, summarize needs an aggregation, and render draws a chart.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Defender for Cloud alerts ingested by the Microsoft Defender for Cloud connector are stored in the SecurityAlert table.
With bi-directional sync enabled, closing the Sentinel incident also closes the original Defender for Cloud alert.
Assigning the Azure Policy for a policy-managed connector requires only the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role.

questions.explain: Defender for Cloud alerts land in SecurityAlert, and bi-directional sync closes the source alert. Policy assignment needs Owner on the assignment scope.

questions.stem: Which table stores events collected by the Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA connector?
options: CommonSecurityLog
Syslog
SecurityEvent
WindowsEvent
questions.explain: CEF messages are parsed into CommonSecurityLog. Plain syslog goes to Syslog, while SecurityEvent and WindowsEvent hold Windows events.

questions.stem: You will use an on-premises Linux server as a log forwarder for firewall CEF logs. Which component must you install before you can target it with a data collection rule?
options: The Log Analytics agent (MMA/OMS)
A Windows Event Collector subscription
The Azure Arc Connected Machine agent
A data collection endpoint on the server
questions.explain: A non-Azure machine needs Azure Arc so the DCR can target it and deploy the Azure Monitor Agent. The Log Analytics agent is retired, WEC is for Windows, and a DCE is an Azure resource, not something you install on the server.

questions.case: A forwarder receives CEF from firewalls on facility local4 and Linux auth logs on facility auth. The engineer created a Syslog via AMA DCR that collects all facilities at LOG_DEBUG, and a CEF via AMA DCR for local4. Firewall events now appear in both the Syslog and CommonSecurityLog tables, which doubles ingestion cost.
questions.stem: What should you do to stop the duplicates?
options: Use different syslog facilities for the Syslog via AMA DCR and the CEF via AMA DCR
Change the forwarder to listen on TCP port 514 only
Move CommonSecurityLog to the data lake tier
Replace the forwarder's Azure Monitor Agent with the Log Analytics agent
questions.explain: When both DCRs collect the same facility, each message is ingested twice. Separate the facilities, for example local4 for CEF and auth for Syslog. Ports, tiers and the retired legacy agent don't fix duplication.

questions.stem: You need to count today's Palo Alto Networks firewall events for each action the firewall took, such as allow or deny. Complete the query.
questions.code:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor == "Palo Alto Networks"
| summarize Events = count() by ____
options: Facility
DeviceAction
EventID
ResultType
questions.explain: DeviceAction is the CommonSecurityLog column for the action the device took. Facility belongs to Syslog, EventID to Windows event tables, and ResultType to sign-in logs.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The Forwarder_AMA_installer.py script configures the syslog daemon to listen on port 514 for both UDP and TCP.
Setting LOG_ERR as a facility's minimum log level also collects LOG_CRIT, LOG_ALERT and LOG_EMERG messages.
The Monitoring Reader role is enough to create the data collection rule.

questions.explain: The installer opens 514 for UDP and TCP. A minimum level includes every more severe level. Creating or editing DCRs needs Monitoring Contributor.

questions.stem: Domain controllers send the All event set, which costs too much. You still need a full user audit trail that includes logon and logoff events. Which event set should you choose?
options: Minimal
Custom with only Event ID 4688
Common
All, with an XPath that excludes Event ID 4624
questions.explain: Common keeps a full user audit trail, including 4624 and 4634, at lower volume. Minimal drops logoff events, 4688 alone is process creation, and excluding 4624 removes logons from the audit trail.

questions.stem: A custom event set must collect only successful and failed logons from the Security log. Complete the XPath query for the data collection rule.
questions.code: ____*[System[(EventID=4624 or EventID=4625)]]
options: Security:
SecurityEvent!
System!
Security!
questions.explain: DCR XPath entries use the form LogName!XPathQuery, so the Security log prefix is 'Security!'. SecurityEvent is a workspace table rather than an event log, and System is a different log.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The Minimal event set includes logoff events (4634).
The Windows Security Events via AMA connector writes events to the SecurityEvent table.
You can test an XPath query locally with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath before adding it to a DCR.

questions.explain: Minimal includes 4624 and 4625 but leaves out 4634. The connector writes to SecurityEvent. Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath checks query syntax and results locally.

questions.stem: You need accounts with more than 20 failed logons, after counting them per account and computer. Complete the query.
questions.code:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| summarize FailedLogons = count() by TargetAccount, Computer
| ____ FailedLogons > 20
options: having
extend
where
distinct
questions.explain: KQL filters aggregated rows with a second where after summarize. HAVING is SQL, not KQL. extend adds a calculated column without filtering, and distinct expects column names.

questions.stem: Workstation security events reach Sentinel through Windows Event Forwarding and the Windows Forwarded Events connector. A built-in rule that queries SecurityEvent never fires for these events. Why?
options: Forwarded events are stored in the WindowsEvent table, not SecurityEvent
WEF subscriptions strip the EventID field
Forwarded events always go to the data lake tier
The rule needs the Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor role
questions.explain: The Windows Forwarded Events connector writes to WindowsEvent. Change the rule to query WindowsEvent, or collect with the Windows Security Events via AMA connector. Event IDs are kept, and tiering and roles aren't the cause.

questions.case: Litware has 6,000 on-premises Windows workstations. Change control forbids installing any additional agents on workstations, but Group Policy changes are allowed. The SOC needs logon and account management events from every workstation in Microsoft Sentinel. Two Windows servers can be dedicated to log collection.
questions.stem: Which collection design should you recommend?
options: Onboard all 6,000 workstations to Azure Arc and deploy AMA with a Windows Security Events DCR
Configure the workstations to send events to a Syslog via AMA forwarder
Have each workstation call the Logs Ingestion API through a scheduled script
Configure WEF by GPO to two Windows Event Collector servers, and collect ForwardedEvents with AMA and the Windows Forwarded Events connector
questions.explain: WEF is built into Windows and is configured by GPO, so agents run only on the collectors. Arc and AMA on every workstation breaks the 'no agents' rule. Syslog can't natively collect Windows event logs, and per-device scripts are fragile.

questions.stem: Events collected through Windows Event Forwarding and the Windows Forwarded Events connector must be searched for account creation (4720). Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where EventID == 4720
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID
options: SecurityEvent
WindowsEvent
Event
ForwardedEvents
questions.explain: The Windows Forwarded Events connector stores data in WindowsEvent. SecurityEvent is used by the Windows Security Events via AMA connector, Event by generic Azure Monitor DCRs, and ForwardedEvents is the Windows log channel name, not a table.

questions.stem: What suffix must the name of a custom log table in a Log Analytics workspace end with?
options: _CF
_CL
_KQL
_Custom
questions.explain: Custom tables end in _CL. _CF is for custom columns added to Azure tables, and _KQL is used for data lake tables created by KQL jobs.

questions.stem: An application uses a Microsoft Entra app registration to send JSON to the Logs Ingestion API and receives 403 Forbidden. The DCR and table are correct. What should you do?
options: Assign Log Analytics Contributor to the app registration on the workspace
Assign Microsoft Sentinel Contributor to the app registration
Create a data collection endpoint and link it to the workspace
Assign the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role to the app registration on the DCR
questions.explain: The Logs Ingestion API checks whether the caller has Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR. Workspace or Sentinel roles don't grant ingestion rights, and a DCE only matters for Private Link or older DCRs.

questions.stem: A DCR for the Logs Ingestion API must drop Debug records and send everything else unchanged to the custom table. Complete the dataFlows fragment.
options: source
input
stream
table
questions.explain: In a DCR transformation, the incoming data is always called 'source'. A plain 'source' passes data through unchanged, and adding operators filters or reshapes it.

questions.stem: You create the destination table for text-file logs that a server writes directly and the Custom Logs via AMA connector collects. Which two columns must the table contain? Select TWO.
options: TenantId
TimeGenerated
SourceSystem
RawData
Computer
questions.explain: The table must have exactly TimeGenerated (datetime) and RawData (string). Message replaces RawData only when logs come through a forwarder. TenantId and SourceSystem are reserved or system columns.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A data collection endpoint (DCE) is always required to use the Logs Ingestion API.
Custom columns added to an Azure (built-in) table must use the _CF suffix.
Clients of the Logs Ingestion API authenticate by using a Microsoft Entra app registration.

questions.explain: A DCE is only needed with Private Link or DCRs that have no logs ingestion endpoint. Custom columns on Azure tables end in _CF. The API uses Entra app authentication with client credentials.

questions.stem: A penetration test runs for two weeks from a known IP address. Incidents that include that IP must be closed automatically during the test only, with no manual clean-up afterwards. What should you configure?
options: A playbook triggered by a scheduled Logic Apps recurrence
A watchlist that disables the affected analytics rules
An automation rule with an expiration date that closes matching incidents
A Data collection rule transformation that drops events from the IP
questions.explain: Automation rules can close incidents that match conditions, and an expiration date disables the rule on its own when the test ends. Dropping the data would hide evidence, and the other options need manual clean-up.

questions.stem: You are creating an automation rule in Microsoft Sentinel. Put the steps in order.
options: Enter a name for the automation rule
Select the trigger, such as When incident is created
Define conditions, such as the analytics rule name or entity values
Add actions, such as change status or run playbook
Set the order and optional expiration, then apply
questions.explain: An automation rule is built in this order: trigger, conditions, then actions. Order and expiration decide when it runs and when it stops.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The When alert is created trigger fires for alerts from Scheduled and NRT analytics rules.
Automation rules that share a trigger run in parallel to reduce latency.
An incident-trigger automation rule can run a playbook that uses the alert trigger.

questions.explain: Alert-created rules cover Scheduled, NRT and Microsoft security rules. Rules run one after another in order. Incident-trigger rules can only run incident-trigger playbooks.

questions.case: An engineer built an incident-trigger playbook in resource group RG-Playbooks. The Sentinel workspace is in RG-SOC. When the engineer creates an automation rule, the playbook appears greyed out and Sentinel reports that it lacks permissions to run it. The engineer is an Owner of both resource groups.
questions.stem: What should you do so the automation rule can run the playbook?
options: Grant Microsoft Sentinel permissions on RG-Playbooks by using Settings > Playbook permissions, signed in as an Owner of that resource group
Assign Logic App Contributor to the engineer on RG-Playbooks
Assign Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator to all SOC analysts
Recreate the playbook as a Standard logic app in the workspace's resource group
questions.explain: Automation rules run playbooks with the Azure Security Insights service account, which needs explicit permission on the playbook's resource group. Granting it requires Owner. More rights for the engineer or the analysts don't help.

questions.stem: During an investigation, an analyst wants to run a playbook against one suspicious IP address shown in the incident, without running it on the whole incident. Which playbook trigger supports this?
options: Microsoft Sentinel alert trigger
Microsoft Sentinel entity trigger
Logic Apps recurrence trigger
HTTP request trigger with an incident ID
questions.explain: The entity trigger lets an analyst run a playbook on a single entity, such as an IP, account or host. The alert trigger acts on an alert, recurrence runs on a schedule, and an HTTP trigger isn't the supported Sentinel integration.

questions.stem: Which three trigger types does the Microsoft Sentinel connector support for playbooks? Select THREE.
options: Workbook
Incident
Watchlist item
Entity
Alert
questions.explain: Sentinel playbooks can be triggered by an incident (including its alerts and entities), an alert or an entity. There are no watchlist or workbook triggers.

questions.stem: Firewall logs must be searchable by analytics rules for 90 days and kept for 7 years for audits, at the lowest cost. How should you configure the CommonSecurityLog table?
options: Analytics retention 7 years
Move the table to the data lake tier and set retention to 7 years
Analytics retention 90 days and total retention 7 years, so older data stays in the data lake tier
Analytics retention 90 days and total retention 90 days
questions.explain: Analytics retention can be at most 2 years, and data lake storage is cheap for long-term retention. Moving the table fully to the data lake stops analytics rules, and 90 days of total retention doesn't meet the 7-year requirement.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Switching a table from the Analytics tier to the Data lake tier stops analytics rules on that table.
Reducing a table's total retention deletes the older data immediately.
Microsoft Sentinel solution tables can be kept in the analytics tier for 90 days without a storage charge.

questions.explain: Data lake-only tables can't feed real-time analytics. Reducing total retention has a 30-day wait before deletion. Sentinel solution tables get 90 days of free analytics retention.

questions.stem: An investigator must search the unified audit log from the Defender portal, and you must grant the least privilege. Which Exchange Online role should you assign?
options: Audit Logs
Mail Recipients
Legal Hold
View-Only Audit Logs
questions.explain: View-Only Audit Logs allows searching the audit log. Audit Logs also allows changing audit settings, so it grants more than needed. Mail Recipients and Legal Hold don't grant audit search.

questions.stem: What is the default retention period for Audit (Standard) records in Microsoft Purview?
options: 90 days
1 year
180 days
10 years
questions.explain: Audit (Standard) keeps records for 180 days. Audit (Premium) keeps Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records for 1 year, and 10 years needs an add-on licence. 90 days applied only to logs created before October 2023.

questions.stem: You need to see Microsoft 365 activity by guest users from the past week in Defender XDR advanced hunting. Complete the query.
questions.code:
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ____ == true
| summarize count() by AccountDisplayName, ActionType
options: IsExternalUser
IsAdminOperation
IsImpersonated
IsAnonymousProxy
questions.explain: IsExternalUser flags accounts from outside the organization. IsAdminOperation marks admin activity, IsImpersonated marks actions done on behalf of another user, and IsAnonymousProxy marks traffic from anonymizing IPs.

questions.stem: CloudAppEvents returns no results in advanced hunting. Which two statements about this table are true? Select TWO.
options: It's populated when Microsoft 365 activities is selected in the Defender for Cloud Apps Microsoft 365 app connector
It's populated only for users with Audit (Premium) licences
It's queried with KQL on the Advanced hunting page of the Defender portal
It's an alias for the Microsoft Entra AuditLogs table
It requires a Microsoft Sentinel workspace onboarded as primary
questions.explain: CloudAppEvents is a Defender XDR advanced hunting table filled by Defender for Cloud Apps. The Microsoft 365 connector must include Microsoft 365 activities. It needs neither Sentinel nor Audit (Premium), and it's separate from Entra AuditLogs.

questions.stem: A Security Copilot workspace was created with its data storage location set to United States. Compliance now requires session data to be stored in the EU. What should you do?
options: Change the data storage location in Owner settings
Set the prompt evaluation location to Europe (EU)
Move the capacity resource to an EU Azure region
Create a new workspace with Europe (EU) as the data storage location
questions.explain: The data storage location can't be changed after a workspace is created. Prompt evaluation location controls where prompts are processed, not where data is stored, and moving capacity doesn't move workspace data.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A single Security Copilot capacity can be used by two workspaces at the same time.
A workspace name can contain spaces, such as 'Contoso SOC'.
The setting that logs Security Copilot activity to Microsoft Purview applies to the whole tenant.

questions.explain: Each capacity serves one workspace at a time. Names can use only letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Audit logging is a tenant-wide setting that a Security Administrator changes.

questions.case: Northwind has 2,000 paid Microsoft 365 E5 user licences and has not bought any Security Copilot capacity. The CISO wants to know how much Security Copilot usage is included each month before deciding whether to provision more capacity.
questions.stem: How many SCUs per month will Northwind receive under the inclusion model?
questions.explain: The inclusion model gives 400 SCUs per month for every 1,000 paid user licences, so 2,000 licences get 800. 10,000 is the monthly cap, and unused SCUs don't roll over.

questions.stem: An analyst has the Copilot contributor role. When they ask Security Copilot to summarize Microsoft Sentinel incidents, the Sentinel plugin returns an access error. What should you do?
options: Assign the analyst the Copilot owner role
Assign the analyst the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role on the Sentinel workspace
Turn on the Sentinel plugin for 'Owners only'
Add more provisioned SCUs to the capacity
questions.explain: Security Copilot works on behalf of the user, so access to Sentinel data needs an Azure role such as Microsoft Sentinel Reader. Copilot owner gives no data access, and plugin scope or SCUs won't fix a permission error.

questions.stem: Which two Microsoft Entra roles automatically inherit Copilot owner access in Security Copilot? Select TWO.
options: Security Operator
Global Reader
Security Reader
Global Administrator
Security Administrator
questions.explain: Global Administrator and Security Administrator, along with roles such as Billing Administrator and Compliance Administrator, inherit Copilot owner. Reader and operator roles don't.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Copilot owner and Copilot contributor are Microsoft Entra directory roles.
If you remove the Everyone group from Security Copilot contributor access, it can't be assigned again.
For new Security Copilot instances, contributor access is given by default to the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group.

questions.explain: Copilot roles belong to Security Copilot and aren't Entra roles. Everyone can't be re-added once removed. New instances default to the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group.

questions.stem: A Copilot owner wants contributors to publish custom plugins for the whole organization, but the organization-scope option isn't shown in Plugin settings. What should the owner do first?
options: Set preinstalled plugin availability to All users
Assign contributors the Security Administrator role
Upload the plugin as an OpenAI plugin
Change the personal-scope custom plugin setting to Contributors and Owners
questions.explain: The organization-scope setting only appears when personal scope lets contributors add their own plugins. The default is Owners only. Preinstalled plugin availability, Entra roles and the plugin type don't control this.

questions.stem: Which two top-level keys must a Security Copilot custom plugin manifest contain?
options: Descriptor and SkillGroups
Name and Endpoints
Plugin and Actions
Metadata and Skills
questions.explain: A Security Copilot plugin manifest, in YAML or JSON, needs Descriptor (name, display name, description) and SkillGroups (the skills and their format). The other pairs aren't the manifest schema.

questions.stem: You need to add a custom Security Copilot plugin for everyone in your organization. Put the steps in order.
options: Select the Sources icon in the prompt bar
In Manage plugins, go to Custom and select Upload plugin
Choose 'Anyone in my organization' and the Security Copilot plugin type
Upload the YAML or JSON manifest, or provide it as a link
Complete any setup fields and select Setup
questions.explain: Custom plugins are added from Sources > Manage plugins > Custom > Upload plugin. Choose the scope and type, provide the manifest, and finish setup.

questions.case: Contoso deployed the Phishing Triage Agent with a new agent identity. Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, unified RBAC, user-reported settings and the 'Email reported by user as malware or phish' alert policy are all in place. Users report phishing every day, but the alerts are closed with no agent verdict.
questions.stem: What should you do so the agent triages these alerts?
options: Assign the agent's identity the Copilot owner role
Replace Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 with Plan 1
Turn off the Auto-Resolve - Email reported by user as malware or phish tuning rule
Turn off the Email reported by user as malware or phish alert policy
questions.explain: The agent can't triage alerts that a tuning rule has already resolved, so disable the built-in auto-resolve rule. The alert policy itself must stay on, Plan 2 is required, and Copilot owner isn't needed by the agent.

questions.stem: The Conditional Access Optimization Agent finds new users who aren't covered by MFA and suggests a new policy. When the suggestion is applied, in what state is the new policy created?
options: Report-only
On
Off
Enforced for administrators only
questions.explain: New policies suggested by the agent are created in report-only mode, so admins can check their impact before turning them on. The agent doesn't change existing policies without approval.

questions.stem: A Copilot owner set up a partner agent from Microsoft Security Store that reads Microsoft Sentinel and Intune data, but the Set up button is disabled. What is required?
options: The owner must add more overage SCUs
A Global Administrator must approve the agent's permissions by using Start approval
The agent must be republished as a custom plugin
Every analyst must be assigned Copilot owner
questions.explain: Partner agents that reach Microsoft products through Microsoft skills need a Global Administrator to approve their permissions before Set up is enabled. SCUs, plugins and analyst roles don't unlock it.

questions.stem: Which two permissions do you need to buy and set up an agent from Microsoft Security Store? Select TWO.
options: Billing Reader on the Azure billing subscription
Contributor or Owner on the Azure billing subscription
Security Reader in Microsoft Entra ID
Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the workspace
Security Copilot owner or contributor
questions.explain: Buying needs Contributor or Owner on the billing subscription, and setting up the agent needs a Security Copilot owner or contributor role. Reader-type roles can't buy or configure agents.

questions.stem: In the Contoso-Compliance workspace only owners may upload knowledge-source files, but in the Contoso-SOC workspace every analyst may. How should you configure this?
options: Set File upload permissions once at tenant level, because the setting applies to all workspaces
Restrict preinstalled plugin availability to Owners only in the compliance workspace
Set File upload permissions in Owner settings separately in each workspace
Assign compliance analysts the Security Reader role in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: File upload permissions (owners only or all contributors) is a per-workspace owner setting. Audit logging is the tenant-wide setting. Plugin availability and Entra roles don't control file uploads.

questions.stem: You are setting up a Microsoft-built Security Copilot agent. Which identity option does Microsoft recommend?
options: Connect your own PIM-eligible Global Administrator account
Use the Copilot capacity's managed identity
Use the Azure Security Insights service account
Create an agent identity (Microsoft Entra Agent ID) scoped to the permissions you grant
questions.explain: A dedicated Entra Agent ID keeps access scoped and manageable. A user account passes on that user's rights, and PIM elevation can make runs fail. The other two identities aren't agent identity options.
